source.title: Inherent Noise in Gradient Based Methods

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; figure values are not numerically reported in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures an optimizer-induced higher-order loss penalty and gradient dot products, but does not measure the train-test gap or test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper’s plotted penalty and dot-product results concern a proposed implicit-regularization mechanism. Numerical values are not stated; the text describes the plotted trends. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures gradient dot products and higher-order training-loss residuals as a proposed implicit-regularization mechanism. It does not test any listed version. The AlexNet test-loss comparison does not establish widening beyond zero training error, and the residual is not magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors interpret simultaneous parameter updates as introducing uncertainty and a higher-order penalty, strongest on updating batches and generally larger in larger models. They propose a possible regularization mechanism; they do not demonstrate improved generalization caused by it. The larger-model ordering can cease late in CIFAR-10 training, and broader architecture, dataset, and regularizer comparisons remain future work.
record.recipe_differences: Measures an optimizer-induced higher-order loss penalty and gradient dot products rather than the interventions or generalization measures in the listed versions; uses fixed learning rates and SGD in its experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The penalty varies by batch recency, model size, training progress, and dataset/architecture setting described in the paper.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher-order training-loss penalties have greater magnitude on updating batches than on recently or long-ago updating batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher-order training-loss residuals depend on batch recency during SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: The updating batch's gradient self-dot-product exceeds its dot products with recently or long-ago updating batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient alignment during SGD depends on batch recency.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger models have higher gradient dot products and larger-magnitude penalties on MNIST and over much of training in the CIFAR-10 comparisons; the CIFAR-10 ordering changes later.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model size and training stage affect first-order gradient contributions and higher-order training-loss residuals.

fits_no_version.finding: The AlexNet gradient-dot-product crossover approximately coincides with AlexNet beginning to overfit in test loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A training-dynamics crossover can coincide with the onset of test-loss overfitting in an architecture comparison.

record.problems: The paper reports trends through figures without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. It does not directly measure generalization gaps in the experiments described in the text; the proposed link to generalization is an interpretation.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under matched natural-label and random-label recipes.
Test-error changes with widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record overstates the absence of generalization measurements: Appendix A.1 and Figure 6 report test loss for AlexNet and small AlexNet. That result still does not test a listed version. States of cannot_determine refer to the listed claims, not to whether the reported mechanism trends appear.

versions.untested_parts: Whether the same recipes fit random labels and generalize on natural labels.
Whether test error keeps decreasing beyond the interpolation threshold. The paper compares model sizes but does not report this outcome in text.
Convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparisons and the role of local connectivity.
Large versus small batch effects on held-out performance.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.

rows.subject: FC 8000
rows.operation_detail: Compared higher-order penalty across updating, recently updating, and long-ago updating batches.

conditions.value: updating, recently updating, long ago updating

rows.value: The text says the updating batch penalty is at least as large in magnitude as the recently updating batch penalty, which is at least as large as the long-ago updating batch penalty.
rows.note: Trend is described in text; figure provides no numeric values.
rows.check: The reported batch-recency ordering is supported, but it measures a higher-order training-loss residual, not an effect named by a claim version.

conditions.value: updating, recently updating, long ago updating

rows.value: The text says the updating batch’s dot product with itself is higher than its dot product with recently or long-ago updating batches.
rows.note: Trend is described in text; figure provides no numeric values.
rows.check: The reported gradient-dot-product ordering is supported but cannot establish any listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: FC networks with 64, 2000, and 8000 nodes
rows.operation_detail: Compared gradient dot products, loss reductions, and higher-order penalties across network sizes during training.

conditions.value: matched by fraction of training-loss reduction

rows.measure: Gradient dot products and magnitude of higher-order penalty
rows.value: The text says larger models have higher dot products and larger-magnitude penalties, while noting the pattern stops being true late in training for more complex datasets.
rows.note: The text describes the size trend for MNIST and qualifies its duration on more complex datasets.
rows.check: Neither test error nor the interpolation threshold is measured. The late-training qualification concerns the more complex datasets, not a demonstrated failure of the MNIST trend. Section 4 describes matching by reduction in training loss; fractional reduction is explicitly specified only for the ResNet comparison.

rows.subject: Alexnet and small Alexnet
rows.size_stated: small Alexnet has one fully connected layer of size 256
rows.operation_detail: Compared dot products, loss reductions, and higher-order penalties during training.
rows.measure: Magnitude of higher-order penalty and gradient dot product
rows.value: The text says Alexnet has larger-magnitude penalty and dot product until training loss is about 1.0; the crossover approximately tracks when Alexnet begins overfitting in test loss.
rows.note: The test-loss comparison is described as a figure-based crossover relation; precise values are not stated.
rows.check: The penalty and dot-product crossover is supported. Appendix A.1 also reports AlexNet beginning to overfit in test loss, but neither zero training error nor continued widening beyond that threshold is established. Both compared models retain convolutional layers, so this is not a V3 comparison.

rows.subject: Resnet 18 and wide Resnet 50
rows.operation_detail: Compared gradient dot products, loss reductions, and higher-order penalties during training.
rows.measure: Magnitude of higher-order penalty and gradient dot product
rows.value: The text says the larger model has more negative penalties for the bulk of training while also having higher dot products.
rows.note: The trend is described in text; figure provides no numeric values.
rows.check: The reported bulk-of-training trend is supported, but the comparison changes depth and width and reports no held-out performance or interpolation threshold.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
